title: Relation Between Polynomial Correlation and Congruence-Preservation Probability
summary: The quantities can each exceed the other, while perfect polynomial correlation implies perfect congruence preservation; a general relation remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a function over an integer ring and a level $\ell$, maximum $\ell$-polynomial correlation $\mathrm{PC}_{\max}^{(\ell)}$ measures its best agreement modulo $p^\ell$ with a polyfunction, while congruence-preservation probability $\mathrm{CPP}(\ell)$ measures the probability of preserving congruence modulo $p^\ell$. Examples show that either $\mathrm{PC}_{\max}^{(\ell)}<\mathrm{CPP}(\ell)$ or $\mathrm{PC}_{\max}^{(\ell)}>\mathrm{CPP}(\ell)$ can occur, although $\mathrm{PC}_{\max}^{(\ell)}=1$ implies $\mathrm{CPP}(\ell)=1$. Determine whether any general relation between these two quantities exists and, if so, characterize and prove it.

scope.domain: This is a mathematical-foundations question about functions over integer rings, polynomial correlation, and congruence preservation.
assumptions: the function is over an integer ring
parameters: ell, the level associated with the two quantities
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether any general relation between maximum ell-polynomial correlation and congruence-preservation probability exists, and if so characterize and prove it.

citations.label: The ABC of Symmetric Primitives over Integer Rings: Milk Before Meat

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents this as an open problem for future work. It gives examples in which either quantity exceeds the other and records only that perfect maximum polynomial correlation implies perfect congruence-preservation probability.
